parts.text: Which claim about this arrangement is correct?

options.text: The two cells make a working battery because opposite terminals touch and together they can run the lamp.
The two cells make a working battery because the $+$ end of one cell touches the $+$ end of the other cell.
Any two cells always make a working battery, even if no terminals touch.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem:
The diagram shows Kabir's two cells joined end to end and wired to a small lamp. The $+$ end of one cell touches the $-$ end of the other cell.

Answer both parts.

part_answers.answer: A working battery joins the positive terminal of one cell to the negative terminal of the next so the lamp can receive electrical energy.

teacher.key_rationale: Opposite terminals must meet for a working multi-cell battery. Same-terminal contact or no contact fails that rule.
teacher.figure_note: Two cells in series with opposite terminals touching, wired to a lamp.
